comment: NPC BEHAVIOUR PROFILES. Vocabulary (which intents exist) is code; character (which intents a creature is allowed, how much it wants each, how far it sees, what range it likes, how often it swings) is this file. A mob sidecar opts in with "behavior": "<name>"; the dev overlay's AI panel switches it at runtime and can write this file back. Hot-reloads on R alongside materials, glyphs and items. The full schema, and the reasoning behind every field, is at the top of src/game/ai_behavior.cpp and src/game/ai_behavior.h.
notes: An intent ABSENT from a profile's "intents" map has weight 0 and is disabled — that is the enable flag, deliberately not a second boolean nobody would keep in sync. An empty profile is a blind, immobile statue, so a creature only ever does what its JSON asked for. Ranges are WORLD VOXELS centre-to-centre (kVoxelMeters = 0.10, so 10 voxels is a metre); cadences are 30 Hz sim TICKS.

profiles.comment: THE SPACING FIXTURE'S PROFILE (src/test/selftest_mob.cpp GateCrowd). Mobile, hostile and it WANTS the target -- which is the whole of what a crowd test needs -- with no `attack` intent and no styles at all, so it walks into the scrum and never swings. It exists because `crowd` is a gate about PERSONAL SPACE and a fixture of four ARMED duelists converging on one point is a knife fight: they are held 3.6 voxels apart by the very feature under test, their swords are 8 voxels long, and they are inside each other's arcs by construction. Measured 2026-09-15, with a sword that finally connects (the sweep's probe no longer dies inside the wielder): 11 attack requests, 54 cut ticks and one of the four dead, on a gate whose spacing numbers were passing perfectly. Friendly fire is `duel`'s subject and it has its own gate; asserting it here made the spacing claim hostage to it. Same reason `training_dummy` exists three entries down.
profiles.name: crowder
profiles.label: Crowder (spacing fixture)

profiles.comment: A dummy of a DIFFERENT FACTION, so a hostile creature will actually pick it as a target. `dummy` is faction "monster" and so is everything that would swing at it, which makes it a training partner nobody attacks. Otherwise identical: blind, passive, immobile.
profiles.name: training_dummy
profiles.label: Training dummy (quarry)

profiles.comment: THE RETREATING QUARRY (src/test/selftest_mob.cpp GateAiPursue). The owner's report turned into a fixture: "enemy mobs need to be able to hit you if you're crouchwalking away from them". A crouching player walks at player.walkSpeed 1.6 m/s x crouchSpeedScale 0.5 = 0.8 m/s = 8 world voxels a second, and the `human` def that gate spawns walks at 31.5 -- so retreatSpeed 0.25 reproduces a crouchwalk on a body the melee sweep can actually cut. A published player ACTOR could not be the subject: it has no limbs to wound and no hp to take off, so a gate built on one would be measuring attack REQUESTS again, which is the half that was never broken.
profiles.//how: It back-pedals FACING the attacker, which is what a retreating player does and is also just holdRange's actuator ("never turn your back to give ground"). The band is 400..420 so every tick of the fight reports "much too close" and the retreat runs at a constant rate instead of tapering as it would near a real band edge. It never swings: no attack intent and no style its library knows. requireLos false so a fixture cannot fail for a line-of-sight flicker at three voxels.
profiles.//speed: retreatSpeed 0.25 IS the crouchwalk the report named, and the gate DOES NOT USE IT: GateAiPursue clones this profile and overrides the number, because measured against a literal crouchwalk the PRE-FIX duelist does fine (it walks at 31.5, so it wins back the twenty-seven voxels its own step-off gives away inside the same cadence that produced them, and the two arms came out level at 12.2 contacts per 100 ticks against 11.9). A fixture that cannot fail measures nothing. The regime the report is really about is a retreat that is a real fraction of the chase, which is the ordinary case in the game rather than an exotic one -- a WALKING player is 16 vox/s against a zombie's 23.5, and a sprinting one is 31.5, which is a human duelist's entire walk speed. The authored 0.25 is kept because it is the honest documentation of the reported scenario and because any other caller wanting "a quarry that gives ground" wants a plausible one.
profiles.name: retreater
profiles.label: Retreating quarry (pursuit fixture)

profiles.comment: A duelist of the OPPOSING faction, so two of them fight. Identical to `duelist` apart from the faction name.
profiles.name: duelist_blue
profiles.label: Duelist (blue)

profiles.//pursuit: A SWING IS A STEP FORWARD (2026-09-16). `pursueSpeed` 0.7 is the fraction of its walk speed this duelist may spend closing WHILE a blow is committed -- before it existed the commit window pinned the mob to `face`, which writes no drive, so it stood perfectly still for 10 ticks and then gave ground for 26 more, and a target simply walking backwards was never in range when the cadence came round. `leadTicks` 15 is where the blow is AIMED: the stroke freezes its target point at the request and every NPC sword cut here is windup 12..14 plus half a cut of 5..7, so the edge arrives about fifteen ticks after the decision and aiming at the present misses by however far you have moved since. Both numbers are per-profile because they are the creature's character -- a zombie leads by 12 and pursues at 0.9 (it does not give ground at all), a static swordsman pursues at 0 and still leads by 14.
profiles.name: duelist
profiles.label: Duelist

profiles.comment: THE WALKING DEAD. Every style it owns is a NATURAL WEAPON (docs/PLAN_impact_unarmed.md), so a disarmed zombie is exactly as dangerous as an armed one -- which is the whole feature: it bites and it punches, and losing a hand costs it one style rather than all of them. It is the first profile whose reach is not the whole story: `bite_lunge` states 22 of its own, and MobSystem::AttackReachOf hands the LONGER of the two to the arbiter, so the creature commits from three body-lengths out and the leap closes the gap. Putting 22 here instead would have it stand off at 22 to punch, which is the coupling the per-style reach exists to break.
profiles.//character: SLOWER AND RECKLESS. A 48-tick cadence against the duelist's 34 (a zombie winds up, it does not fence), a band that starts INSIDE the duelist's (2..7 against 7..11) and almost no retreat or circling -- the dead do not give ground and they do not look for an angle. `disengageTicks` 0 for the same reason: a duelist hits and steps off, a zombie hits and keeps coming. Sight is shorter (34) and the fov is the full 360, because it does not need to be looking at you.
profiles.name: zombie
profiles.label: Zombie
profiles.//attack: aimTolerance 0.55 -> 0.95 and cadence 48 -> 40 (2026-09-19). THE CONE IS HOW FAR OFF ITS NOSE A THING MAY BE AND STILL BE ATTACKED, and a zombie is the creature with the least business being fussy about it: 0.55 rad is a 63-degree window that a target sidestepping at contact range leaves in a handful of ticks, so the cadence came up and nothing came out of it. 0.95 is most of a hemisphere in front, which is also what the bite's own lateral sweep now covers -- the two are the same claim about how wide the mouth's approach is, one at the decision and one at the stroke. The cadence comes down with it because a swing that is now allowed to be thrown is one the creature should be throwing: 40 ticks is 1.33 s between attempts, still far slower than the duelist's 34.

profiles.comment: THE SNAKE (assets/mobs/snake.json, docs/PLAN_weapon_coats.md package D). An ambusher: with nothing in sight it WANDERS (`movement.wander`: legs of a slow slither to points within 24 voxels of where it was born, each followed by a 3..12 s rest lying coiled -- the slither keeps its curve when the body stops), closes on anything of another faction that comes within sight, holds off at striking distance and throws `snake_strike`, its one style. Ranges are centre-to-centre and a snake's centre is nine voxels behind its own fangs, which is why the band (9..12) looks wide for a creature this small.
profiles.//character: STRIKE AND DRAW BACK. A 45-tick cadence, a short commit and a real disengage: a snake bites and recoils rather than standing in the fight, and the venom (the bite block in the sidecar) is what does the work afterwards. Sight 30 with the full 360: it feels you coming through the ground.
profiles.name: snake
profiles.label: Snake

profiles.comment: THE FIRST PROFILE BUILT FROM RULES (2026-09-24). Everything it does beyond standing still is a rule: its authored `flee` weight is 0, so it only runs while one of the rules below holds, and it runs from whatever set it off -- the nearest creature of another faction it can see, or straight on when there is none (on fire, nothing in sight). Nothing ships with it; put "behavior": "skittish" in a sidecar to get a creature that bolts. The `ai-rules` gate drives it.
profiles.//rules: A rule is { when: { fact: test, ... }, weight: { intent: w }, scale: { intent: k } }. ALL the tests must hold; while they do, `weight` replaces the intent's authored weight and `scale` multiplies it, rule by rule in order. Facts: hp (0..1 of authored life), burning (0..1 of limbs alight), limbsLost, sinceHurt (ticks since life last fell, 1e9 = never), hasTarget, visible, targetDist, allies, enemies (live actors of our / another faction within sightRange). Tests: "<0.3", "<=", ">", ">=", "==", "!=", a bare number or a bool (==). An unknown fact or intent drops the whole rule and says so in the load log.
profiles.name: skittish
profiles.label: Skittish (flees)

rules.note: something of another faction close by: keep away
hurt in the last three seconds: run hard
on fire: run

profiles.comment: THE FIGHTING STYLES (2026-09-27). Five humans who fight a PERSON rather than a dummy: each reads its own body (hp, limbs, just-hurt), its own weapon (armed, myReach) and its opponent (targetArmed, reachAdv, targetAttacking / targetRecovering / targetGuarding, targetHp) and changes HOW it fights through rule `tune`s, and each answers your swings with the `guard` / `dodge` verbs gated by `defense` (a per-blow skill roll plus a reaction delay, so a quick blow beats a slow reader). `feintChance` fakes a swing and pulls out; `riposteTicks` is the counter after a blow it saw through; `flank` + the pressRank rule make several of them surround you and take turns instead of queueing in a line. Every one is written to work with ANY weapon or none: an unarmed rule is part of each. The AI panel's 'fighting styles' buttons and the random human spawn these.
profiles.//swordsman: THE ALL-ROUNDER. Trades when its own blow is ready (attack 3.0 beats guard 2.6), guards when it is not, ripostes 4 ticks after a blow it covered. Reads the matchup: out-reached it closes fast past your point; out-reaching you it kites (keepOut); against an empty-handed target it presses; a guarding target gets feints and an angle. Hurt, it stands off and covers more; badly hurt and losing, it breaks and runs for a few seconds after each wound.
profiles.name: swordsman
profiles.label: Swordsman

rules.note: empty-handed: get inside and brawl, weave instead of blocking
out-reached: close past the point quickly and stay close
out-reaching it: make it come onto my point
it has nothing in its hands: press
it just swung: punish the recovery
it is covering: bait it and find an angle
hurt: fight from further out, cover more
a limb gone: slower, sloppier
just took a wound: step off
badly hurt and losing: break off after every wound
two of us already on it: circle and wait my turn

profiles.//fencer: THE KITER. Thrusts from the edge of its reach and stands just outside yours (base keepOut 1.5), circles a lot, and answers a blow with a quick DODGE rather than a block (dodge 2.8 vs guard 1.4). Feints often and ripostes fast. When YOU out-reach IT, kiting is impossible, so it switches: drops the keep-out and darts in. Hurt, it reads you better and stands further off.
profiles.name: fencer
profiles.label: Fencer

rules.note: empty-handed: dart in and out
out-reached: kiting is impossible, get inside
it just swung: lunge into the gap
it is covering: feint it open
it is weak: close the distance
hurt: sharper, further off
badly hurt and losing: disengage and run
the front is crowded: work the flank

profiles.//brawler: THE CLOSE FIGHTER. Lives inside your reach: a tight band, a fast cadence, a short step-off and a lot of pursuit. Blocks little and weaves a lot. With a weapon it stands a little further out; out-reached, it charges straight in. Punishes a whiff hard. Getting hit makes it ANGRIER (faster cadence), and badly hurt it gets sloppy rather than careful.
profiles.name: brawler
profiles.label: Brawler

rules.note: holding a weapon: stand where it lands
out-reached: charge straight in
it just swung: pile in
it is covering: batter it
just got hit: angry
badly hurt: sloppy and wild
someone else is in its face: wait for an opening

profiles.//berserker: RELENTLESS. Almost no defence, no retreat, no step-off, a short cadence and full pursuit. It does not get careful when hurt -- it gets FASTER: under half life it swings more often and moves quicker and stops defending at all. It goes for the kill on a weakened target. Never flees and ignores the press queue: it does not wait its turn.
profiles.name: berserker
profiles.label: Berserker

rules.note: blood rage: faster, reckless, no defence
nearly dead: everything into the next blow
it is weak: finish it
it just swung: straight through it
it is covering: batter the guard

profiles.//guardian: THE TURTLE. Keeps its guard up whenever it stands in reach of an armed enemy (guardStance 0.6), reads blows well (skill 0.65, 6 ticks: a wall, not an unbeatable one -- at 0.8 / 5 it lost 4 hp to a duelist that lost 300), always prefers to block (guard 3.4 over attack 3.0), and counters: a covered blow earns a 2-tick riposte and a whiff is punished at a third of the cadence. Slow to commit otherwise. Empty-handed it cannot block, so it dodges and closes. Hurt, it turtles harder. Beside allies it holds its ground rather than circling.
profiles.name: guardian
profiles.label: Guardian

rules.note: empty-handed: cannot block, so weave and close
it just swung: counter
it has nothing in its hands: stop covering, press
out-reached: shuffle inside behind the guard
hurt: turtle
with allies: hold the line
not my turn: shield up at the edge

profiles.comment: AN AUTHORED VILLAGER (PLAN_world_editor P7, world/refs_npc.h). Every `npc` ref gets this unless its props.behavior says otherwise. Its DAY is the six activity verbs (sleep / work / wander / socialize / eat / goto): the resident layer writes the schedule row's verb and the next place to put its feet onto the brain, and they score a flat 1 x 0.6 here -- so anything below that outweighs the day. PASSIVE TO STRANGERS: aggro `neutral` picks no target until it is hurt, then for provokeTicks it answers the nearest stranger (whoever named IT as their target first) with its fists. FLEES HOSTILES: the `hostiles` fact counts creatures whose own profile is aggro hostile (a zombie, not the player), and the rule lets flight (2.0) beat both the day and a fight it is not winning.
profiles.name: villager
profiles.label: Villager

rules.note: a monster in sight: run from it
badly hurt in a fight: run

profiles.comment: THE IMP (docs/PLAN_demons.md D1; assets/mobs/demon/imp_skerrick.json, assets/demons/skerrick.json). A summoned thing that wants its summoner dead: faction `demon`, aggro hostile, the full 360 (it was looking for you before it arrived). AGILE AND LIGHT: a short fast cadence of claw rakes and bites (the human's natural weapons; demon.js makes the fists cut), a close band it darts in and out of, a lot of circling and a quick dodge. Ranges are centre-to-centre in world voxels and an imp is under a metre tall, so every number is about half a man's. CONTAINMENT IS NOT HERE: a demon summoned into an intact salt circle keeps this profile and keeps wanting you; the circle (game/demon_circle.h) clamps its walk and refuses a blow across the ring.
profiles.name: imp
profiles.label: Imp
profiles.//cast: D4 (game/demon_cast.h): an imp casts SPARINGLY -- a firebolt (twice as likely) or a gust every six to nine seconds when it can see you between 6 and 44 voxels off. It does not blink: the verb is in the kit (assets/demons/spells/blink.json) for demons that know it, and an imp that could would leave every circle without quicksilver. Spell names are assets/demons/spells/ stems; a repeat weighs the draw. Its own small pool (mana / regenPerMille), never its blood. Contained in a circle it cannot claw across, this is how it still reaches you -- unless D3's sulfur severs `cast_out`.

rules.note: it just swung: dart in
badly hurt: skitter off and come again

profiles.comment: THE FIEND, a GREATER DEMON's fighting character (docs/PLAN_demons.md D4; body assets/mobs/demon/fiend.*, demon.js's `fiend` preset, 2 m). Near-certain death for an unprepared player, and every number that makes it so is HERE and in assets/demons/spells/: a full kit (hellfire twice over, firebolt, lava under your feet, lift-then-drop, a gust, a fire ward on itself, a blink to close), a deep fast-filling pool, a cadence of two to three seconds, three carriers in the air. Not an instant kill: no single kit spell's blast exceeds demonCast.maxBlastPower (gate demon-cast). In melee it is a long-reaching brute that does not give ground.
profiles.name: fiend
profiles.label: Fiend

profiles.comment: A RELEASED IMP (docs/PLAN_demons.md D3; assets/demons/skerrick.json `released`). The imp profile with aggro neutral: let out of a circle whose binding HELD, he wants nobody until struck. A stand-in for D5's contract, which will say what a released demon does. If the binding fails on release he keeps `imp` (hostile) instead.
profiles.name: imp_bound
profiles.label: Imp (released)

rules.note: it just swung: dart in
badly hurt: skitter off and come again
